introduction: On this Sunday, the prophet Habakkuk cries out to God in a time of violence, and God answers that the righteous will live by faith. In the Gospel, the apostles ask Jesus, Increase our faith, and he tells them that faith the size of a mustard seed can do great things, and that we are servants who do our duty. Paul urges Timothy to stir into flame the gift of God. Let us ask for a living faith.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the righteous live by faith. Let us bring our prayers to the Lord.
intentions: For the Church: that her faith may be strong and humble in times of trial. Let us pray to the Lord.
For bishops, priests and deacons: that they may stir into flame the gift they received by the laying on of hands. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who cry out to God in times of violence and injustice: that they may not lose hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose faith is weak or wavering: that the Lord may increase their faith. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may serve the Lord faithfully and humbly, without seeking reward. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, the righteous live by faith. Increase our faith, stir up the gifts you have given us, and make us faithful servants of your Kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Increase our faith
reflection.body:
Habakkuk lives in a violent time, and he complains to God with honesty: "LORD, how long will I cry, and you will not hear?" Many believers have prayed this prayer. God's answer does not explain everything, but it gives a promise and a way to live. "Write the vision, and make it plain." It will come, even if it seems slow: "Though it takes time, wait for it." And then a sentence that Paul will later quote: "the righteous will live by his faith."

In the Gospel, the apostles ask Jesus, "Increase our faith." Jesus does not tell them they need more faith. He tells them that even a little real faith is powerful: "If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree," Be uprooted and be planted in the sea, "and it would obey you." What matters is not the size of our faith but the greatness of the God we trust.

Then Jesus tells a short parable about a servant who comes in from the fields and serves his master's dinner before eating himself. The servant does not expect special thanks for doing his job. "Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say," We are unworthy servants; we have done our duty. Faith is not a way of earning credit with God. It is a humble trust that serves without counting.

Paul writes to Timothy, who seems discouraged: "stir up the gift of God which is in you." And he reminds him: "For God didn't give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control."

This week, pray the apostles' simple prayer every day: Lord, increase our faith. And do your daily duties for God, without seeking thanks, trusting that he sees.
